author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: The Library of America's omnibus of five PKD novels from his most productive decade — the volume that marked his admission into the American literary canon.
page_summary:
This is a collected omnibus edition, not a single novel. It gathers five works from PKD's peak period — including Martian Time-Slip, Dr. Bloodmoney, Now Wait for Last Year, Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said, and A Scanner Darkly — chosen to represent the range of his 1960s and 70s output.

The grouping matters as much for what it signifies as for what it contains. The Library of America is the institution that canonizes American literature, and its multi-volume Dick editions in the 2000s certified a writer once confined to the SF pulps as a permanent part of the national literature. The selection spans PKD's reality-breakdown novels, his post-nuclear and time-distortion books, and the drug-and-surveillance dread of A Scanner Darkly, tracing the decade in which he did his most sustained and inventive work.
